audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3 (Levels 4-5), 4 (Level 6) and 6 (2+ items) disagree with the packet, with this page's own why-strings, and with the mirror.
audit.why: whys[3] literally begins 'Skill stage' but the row reads Jax. whys[4] ends 'so he owns 6' but the row reads Lillia. whys[6] describes your kite and DoT out-scaling him but the row reads Jax. The mirror already corrected the same three rows on the Jax page.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Lillia / Skill / Jax / Skill / Jax / Jax / Lillia in both layers, ratings moved with it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears on the page despite Counter Strike being named the clock the lane runs on.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — 17 seconds at rank 1, one of the longest punish windows any top laner gives up. Leap Strike is 8s at 700 range, Empower 7s at rank 1, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110s, and Lilting Lullaby 150s. 'Commit on its cooldown' means nothing without the number.
audit.corrected: 17s written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], both do's, whys[0]-derived phases text and wants.you[0]; 110s and 150s into the level 6 lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings tell the reader to 'hold your damage' into Counter Strike, as if it blanks Lillia's whole kit.
audit.why: Riot's text: Jax 'dodges all incoming ATTACKS for a short duration and then quickly counterattacks, stunning all surrounding enemies'. It dodges basic attacks. Blooming Blows, Watch Out! Eep! and Swirlseed are abilities and land through it in full — including the true-damage outer edge. Telling Lillia to stop damaging him entirely for 17 seconds throws away the majority of her damage for no reason; the correct instruction is to withhold autos and keep casting.
audit.corrected: 'Attacks, not abilities' written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], dosFull[0].d, whys[2], spikes[1], wants.you[1] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings call his ultimate 'Grandmaster's Might' and say it 'triples his defensive stats'.
audit.why: His R is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Riot's text: every third consecutive attack deals additional MAGIC damage, and activating it deals damage around him and increases Armor and Magic Resist for a short duration. No tripling is stated anywhere. A fabricated name plus an invented magnitude on the single most important spike in the lane.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster-at-Arms named, described as armour, MR and a third-attack magic proc, with its 110s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late are written in first person — 'mine', 'I', 'me' throughout.
audit.why: The site is in second-person coaching voice; three of the longest strings on the page break it.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person at the same length.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact.
audit.why: Riot's text says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target; it creates nothing.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are mine because Jax has no E Counter Strike yet — I sit at max range, hit the outer-edge Q sweetspot, roll E Swirlseed for the slow, and start the Dream Dust burn that he simply can't dodge. The Q move speed stacks keep me a step outside his Q-W gap-close, so every time he walks up he just eats more DoT. The moment he hits 3 and holds Counter Strike, stop auto-trading into him — that dodge-then-stun is the one button that turns my hop-in into a kill, so chip with the DoT and don't feed the parry.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours because Jax has no Counter Strike yet — sit at max range, hit the outer-edge Q sweetspot, roll Swirlseed for the slow, and start the Dream Dust burn he simply cannot dodge. Your move-speed stacks keep you a step outside Leap Strike's 700 range, so every walk-up costs him more DoT. The moment he hits 3 and holds Counter Strike, stop auto-trading — it dodges attacks for its duration, then stuns everything around him, so keep casting spells, which it does not stop, and never feed it your autos.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are close: my full-rank Q and compounding burn want to grind him down, but a held Counter Strike still punishes any greedy step-up, so I poke and let the DoT do the work rather than committing autos into his dodge window. At 6 the lane tilts to him — Grandmaster's Might triples his defensive stats and his duel takes off, so my Lilting Lullaby is a disengage tool here, not an all-in. Sleep him to peel a gank or break his W-empowered burst, never to start a fight I'll lose under his R.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are close: full-rank Q and the compounding burn want to grind him, but a held Counter Strike still punishes a greedy auto, so poke and let the DoT work — your spells land through the dodge, your attacks do not. At 6 the lane tilts to him: Grandmaster-at-Arms adds armour, MR and a magic proc on every third attack, so Lilting Lullaby is a disengage here, not an all-in. Sleep him to peel a gank or break an Empower burst, never to open a fight under his R.

edits.before: Late game flips back to me. Once I'm at 2+ items with Liandry's/Riftmaker, my W and Dream Dust deal real percent-HP damage and I stop ever walking into Counter Strike — I kite, stack the burn, and isolate-sleep him with R while he can't close the gap. His single-target duel needs to catch me, and my passive plus Q move speed mean he never does; just don't get caught flat-footed against his Q-W onto a teammate, and never face him in a corridor where the dodge-stun connects.
edits.after: Late game flips back to you. At 2+ items with Liandry's or Riftmaker your W and Dream Dust deal real percent-HP and you stop walking into Counter Strike at all — kite, stack the burn, and isolate-sleep him while he cannot close the gap. His single-target duel has to catch you, and Blooming Blows' stacking move speed means it never does. Just don't get caught flat-footed when he Leap Strikes a teammate, and never fight him in a corridor where the dodge-stun connects.

notes: The most valuable correction on this page: Counter Strike dodges ATTACKS, not abilities. Six strings told the reader to hold ALL damage for its duration, which throws away Blooming Blows, Watch Out! Eep! and Swirlseed — the bulk of Lillia's damage — for 17 seconds at rank 1 for no reason. The correct rule is 'hold the autos, keep casting'. Second: his ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms, not 'Grandmaster's Might', and Riot's text gives armour, MR and a third-attack magic proc — nothing about tripling defensive stats. Chart flips match the mirror's three rows and are one atomic group with their ratings. early/mid/late were in first person and are now second.
